summary: The G and 2D shifts are real (not calibration) and scale with laser power. Their most likely cause is laser heating, not a doping change. Strain is not excluded but cannot be separated from heating with these three spectra. For absolute G/2D positions, trust the 0.5 mW spectrum (least laser-perturbed), with caveats: it was taken first in the sequence, so exposure history is confounded with power, and it has the lowest signal-to-noise. Single-layer identity is consistent with I2D/IG ≈ 3.0 and a single Lorentzian 2D band, but substrate and laser dependence keep that from being definitive. No D band is detected, so defect density is low. Fits were done with numpy/lmfit in this folder; the skill's scripts and reference notes sit outside the working folder, which the system prompt excludes, so they were not used, and the literature values below are recalled and unverified.

observations.finding: G and 2D both soften monotonically with power at a fixed spot; the shift is not a calibration offset because the Si 520 line is constant across the three spectra.
Slope ratio of 2D to G shift is 2.85±0.18, which lies between the strain-type and doping-type ratios I recall from the literature but is not decisive.
observations.evidence: dω2D/dωG = (-5.13±0.05)/(-1.80±0.11) = 2.85±0.18 (0.5 to 5 mW). Recalled literature values: about 2.2 for uniaxial strain and about 0.7 for electron/hole doping (Mohiuddin et al., PRB 79, 205433 (2009); Das et al., Nat. Nanotechnol. 3, 210 (2008)). I did not check these figures in this session.
observations.source: Mohiuddin et al., Phys. Rev. B 79, 205433 (2009) and Das et al., Nat. Nanotechnol. 3, 210 (2008) — values recalled, figure/table not checked

observations.finding: Intensity ratios point against a doping change with power: I2D/IG (peak-height ratio) is constant, and G and 2D intensities scale linearly with power, as does the Si line.
observations.evidence: I2D/IG height ratio = 2.95, 3.01, 2.98 (0.5, 2, 5 mW). G height ratio to 0.5 mW = 1.00, 3.95, 9.91. 2D height ratio = 1.00, 4.02, 10.0. Si area ratio = 1.00, 4.22, 10.66 (roughly linear, slightly superlinear for Si).

observations.finding: Linewidths broaden with power for both G and 2D, consistent with laser heating (anharmonic phonon broadening); the D band is absent, so defects are not the cause of the broadening.
observations.evidence: G FWHM 13.74±0.44, 15.71±0.29, 17.91±0.23 cm-1. 2D FWHM 32.0±0.3, 34.8±0.2, 39.3±0.1 cm-1. D-band fit at fixed 1350 cm-1: area 65±167 (0.5 mW), consistent with zero; 4868±12444 (5 mW), unconstrained. Upper bound I_D/I_G ≲ 0.01 at 0.5 mW from 3σ of the area over G area 51515.

observations.finding: The power dependence is not linear. Most of the 2D shift occurs between 0.5 and 2 mW, which could indicate an exposure-history or sequencing artifact rather than heating alone.
observations.evidence: Weighted linear fit of 2D vs power gives slope -0.91±0.01 cm-1/mW with residuals +1.12, -0.60, +0.09 cm-1. Step 0.5→2 mW: -3.09 cm-1 (-2.1 cm-1/mW). Step 2→5 mW: -2.04 cm-1 (-0.7 cm-1/mW). G is closer to linear: slope -0.39±0.02 cm-1/mW, residuals ≤0.05 cm-1.

observations.finding: Zero-power limit (linear extrapolation) for G is about 1581.4 cm-1 with small uncertainty; for 2D about 2669 cm-1, poorly constrained by a linear model.
observations.evidence: Linear weighted intercept: G 1581.44±0.08 cm-1; 2D 2668.85±0.04 cm-1 with large residuals, so the 2D intercept is model-dependent. Measured 0.5 mW values (1581.29, 2669.51) are upper bounds on the unperturbed positions for heating-induced shifts.

observations.finding: Layer number is consistent with single-layer graphene but not confirmed by this data alone.
observations.evidence: Single-Lorentzian 2D band with FWHM about 32 cm-1 at 0.5 mW; I2D/IG height ratio about 3.0, constant across powers. Comparison with a published monolayer I2D/IG threshold would need a reference paper, which I did not verify.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: low (D band absent, I_D/I_G ≲ 0.01 at 0.5 mW)

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: undetermined (not separable from heating with these spectra)

properties.name: doping_type
properties.value: undetermined (I2D/IG constant with power argues against power-induced doping change, but absolute doping not determined)

caveats: Sequential acquisition: the spectra were taken one after another in the order 0.5, 2, 5 mW (as labelled); power and exposure history are confounded. Photo-induced doping or adsorbate desorption can change G and 2D in an irreversible way, which heating does not. Repeating 0.5 mW after 5 mW would test this.

Background is not linear in power: median background (1800-2000, 2100-2400, 2900-3100 cm-1) is about 190/350/200 at 0.5 mW, 350/310/280 at 2 mW and 2100/2500/3550 at 5 mW. The 5 mW spectrum also has the highest noise (about 104 vs 22 at 0.5 mW). This suggests different acquisition settings or an added luminescence background; it does not move the fitted G and 2D positions by more than 0.03 cm-1 across window and baseline choices.

Spectrum sampling differs (step 1.05, 1.01, 0.97 cm-1 per point) with the same 450-3199 cm-1 range, so the three files were resampled or recorded with different point counts. Positions were fit on the native grids.

Calibration: the Si line sits at about 520.9 cm-1, about +0.2 cm-1 above the commonly quoted room-temperature value of 520.7 cm-1 (recalled, not checked). The offset is the same in all three spectra, so shifts are unaffected but absolute positions should be read with about 0.2 cm-1 offset.

Excitation dependence: the 2D position depends on laser energy (dispersion about 100 cm-1/eV, Ferrari et al., PRL 97, 187401 (2006), recalled), so absolute 2D positions at 532 nm cannot be compared with values at other wavelengths without correction.
Heating coefficients: the temperature coefficients for G and 2D needed to turn the shift into a temperature rise are not verified here, so I cannot convert the measured shifts to a temperature.
Substrate: SiO2/Si was taken from the user's description; oxide thickness, and therefore interference enhancement and I2D/IG, were not provided.
questions_for_user: What was the acquisition order and integration time per spectrum? If the sequence was 0.5, 2, 5 mW as labelled, the 0.5 mW spectrum is the least laser-exposed; re-measure 0.5 mW after 5 mW to test whether the shifts are reversible (heating) or persistent (photo-doping or desorption).
Are the three spectra identical in accumulations and grating? The background and noise differ strongly between them (especially 5 mW) and the point spacing differs.
What is the oxide thickness and is there an unstrained or known reference (e.g. a bilayer or a flake from the same chip)? Without a reference, absolute strain and doping cannot be fixed.
Was the sample temperature controlled, and was the laser power measured at the sample (not just nominal)?
Was polarization analysed? Strain would split or broaden the G band in polarized spectra; a single unpolarized spectrum cannot show that.

Skill scripts and reference notes (ramanlens raman-analysis) are located outside the working folder, which the system prompt excludes, so they were not run or read; all fitting was done with numpy/lmfit directly on the three CSVs.

Heating versus strain separation: the measured 2D/G slope ratio (2.85±0.18) cannot distinguish them, since laser heating also produces thermal-expansion strain on SiO2. The sequential acquisition confounds time-dependent doping with power.
Cannot determine absolute strain or doping from the 532 nm positions without an unstrained reference and the 2D excitation-energy dispersion.
Layer number and defect density come from single-spot intensity ratios, which depend on substrate interference and laser energy; they are indicative, not definitive.
The 2D power dependence is non-linear over three points, so the zero-power extrapolation for 2D (about 2669 cm-1) is uncertain by at least 0.5 cm-1.
